name: Holy Mission
english_description: A large (~24,000 .lpc file), heavily player-authored MudOS-lineage fantasy world originally run out of Linz, Austria (the login banner reads 'Welcome to the Holy Mission at Linz, Austria'). Character creation is a straight race pick across seven Tolkien-flavored races -- human, elf, half-elf, dwarf, hobbit, orc, and troll -- each with its own short lore blurb straight from the archive's own doc/races files (hobbits explicitly called out as natural thieves for their agility, orcs as 'usually an evil race' but not fixed-alignment, trolls as large, slow, inately-evil brutes), feeding into five class guilds each split into three sub-specializations: priest (druid/shaman/monk), adventurer (ranger/vagabond/jedi), mage (fire/water/earth/air elemental), fighter (barbarian/berserker/samurai), and thief (pirate/ninja/assassin). The adventurers' guild runs a real fetch quest ('Retrieve the Orc slayer from the evil orc shaman, and give it to Leo'). The starting village radiates out from a church consecrated to 'Illuvatar' (a direct Tolkien reference) that revives the dead at its own altar, with a churchyard, sewers, a guard house, bank, shops, and the guildhouse nearby, plus a separate orc valley, forest, mines, and a whole distinct 'south' region -- extensive player/wizard-authored content built up over years of individual work (the archive's own comments date from the early-to-mid 1990s onward). Confirmed MudOS/FluffOS-compatible via a full-tree driver_hook/set_driver_hook/H_[A-Z_]+ grep (zero hits) before porting. Bringing it online required substantial recovery work: two of the archive's most important base classes (sys/living.lpc, sys/player.lpc) were preserved as empty 0-byte files, with the real ~3500+ line implementations misfiled under doc/lib/ as if they were documentation; doc/lib/player.lpc doesn't even inherit doc/lib/living.lpc, independently duplicating dozens of stat/state fields and helper functions ported verbatim from its sibling. The single most severe and novel bug found (AGENTS.md §7.177): a direct, explicit call to a function literally named 'reset' can silently execute as a no-op on this driver even when called eagerly from that very object's own create() -- broke both character stat initialization (score crashed on every new character) and the password database itself (every registered password silently lost across a driver restart) -- fixed by renaming the real logic to do_reset() and keeping reset() as a thin pass-through. A related corpus-wide-shaped bug: this driver's 1800-second 'time to reset' left a brand-new character's own starting room completely dark and undescribed for up to half an hour, fixed at the universal room base class. Full technical detail (including §7.178's wizard-database seeding bug) is in NOTES.md and AGENTS.md. Verified live end to end: registration, gender + race pick (stats update correctly), arrival in a fully lit and described starting room, the church, save/quit/reconnect across a full driver restart with race/stats/guild intact, and a wrong password correctly rejected.
